_comment: digperiphs wound-SoC configuration: the Castalia defaults with (1) the four Castalia-Quad AFE register stubs + the shared EIS engine stub dropped (peripherals.cqAfeStubs=false) and the QSPI0 flash controller instantiated in their place (peripherals.qspi=true, page-0 slot 12 @0x4C00; vectors 55/56), (2) the I3C0 controller instantiated in the MUTEX page sub-slot 1 (peripherals.i3c=true, @0x6100; vectors 86-93), (3) the NFC0 ISO 14443A tag engine instantiated in the MUTEX page sub-slot 2 (peripherals.nfc=true, @0x6200; vectors 94-97), and (4) the RTC0 real-time clock instantiated in the MUTEX page sub-slot 5 (peripherals.rtc=true, @0x6500; vector 114). I3C or NFC tightens the mutex-bank decode to its 256 B sub-slot 0; with I3C+NFC the IRQ source list grows to 98 (meip stays frozen at slot 85; I3C 86-93, NFC 94-97) and a 4th glitch-filter instance appears, and enabling RTC0 grows the source list further to 115 (vector 114 = RTC0's single combined alarm/tick source; NUM_EN_WORDS stays 4). NFC's digital AFE / RF interface is off-die (placeholder-tied); RTC0 is zero-pin (ungated lfxt_in wall clock, CDC/flags/IRQ on the free-running MCLK). QSPI and AFE stubs are mutually exclusive (both claim page-0 slot 12); I3C, NFC, and RTC are independent of both and of each other. Everything else is default (the NPU stays ON). Prove with: make verify CONFIG=config/wound.json
